transcript.text: Elena, on your question about regulatory risk — yes, there is a meaningful risk if we initiate customer notifications before the Form R-17 is filed. The Form R-17 is a voluntary correction report, and the regulator will expect our customer notification timeline to be presented as part of that filing's corrective-action plan. If we notify customers before submitting the form, we risk creating an inconsistency between what we've told customers and what we've told the regulator, and the regulator could view pre-filing notifications as premature corrective action taken outside the voluntary correction framework. That said, I see the tension: Nadia's 14-day notification clock is a hard deadline, and we don't yet know when the regulator's written acknowledgment will arrive to unblock my call note. I'd recommend we prepare the notification materials now, as you've authorized, but hold on sending them until the Form R-17 is filed. If it becomes clear that the acknowledgment is going to delay us past the point where we can meet the 14-day deadline, I'd want to revisit this discussion and potentially contact the intake attorney again to see whether there's a pathway to file or get conditional approval to notify in advance. I don't want to commit to that approach today, but I want us to have it as a contingency.
